newsitem.title: USA: US oil demand up 3.3 pct in June from year ago - API.
newsitem.headline: US oil demand up 3.3 pct in June from year ago - API.

text.p: U.S. demand for petroleum products rose 3.3 percent in June from the same month a year ago, boosted by growth in demand for distillates and kerosene jet fuel, the American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday.
Deliveries of oil products in June averaged 18.67 million barrels per day, up from 18.11 million in June 1996, it said.
In its monthly statistics, the API also said U.S. imports of crude oil and petroleum products rose 4.3 percent in June from a year ago to average 10.37 million bpd, surpassing May's record high.
June crude oil imports rose to nearly 8.5 million bpd, surpassing May's volume and marking a shift from products imports.
U.S. crude production in June slipped 2.5 percent from a year ago to average 6.30 million bpd.
Gasoline deliveries in June rose 2.1 percent from a year ago to average 8.25 million bpd.
Distillate fuel deliveries jumped 6.3 percent in June from a year ago to average 3.39 million bpd, on strong economic growth and transportation demand.
Kerosene jet fuel deliveries gained 4.6 percent in June from a year ago to average 1.63 million bpd, continuing their rebound on seasonal, non-aviation demand, the API said.
Residual fuel demand rose 2.9 percent in June from a year ago to average 756,000 bpd, as warmer-than-normal weather on the East Coast boosted air conditioning demand.
Demand for other oils gained 2.6 percent from a year ago to average 4.74 million bpd, boosted by petrochemical feedstock demand.
Refinery use averaged 97.3 percent of capacity in June, up from 96.4 percent in June 1996.
